statement: On a number line, point P is at 2.5 and point Q is at 4.1. Point R lies between them, one quarter of the way from P to Q. Where is R?

choices.misconception: I found how far R is from P and gave that distance instead of R's position.
I measured the quarter of the distance from P in the wrong direction, away from Q.
I wrote one quarter of 1.6 as 0.04 instead of 0.4 and added it to 2.5.
I found the point halfway between P and Q instead of a quarter of the way.

hints: How far apart are P and Q?
Find the distance from P to Q by subtracting. Take one quarter of that distance, then step that far from P towards Q.
The distance is 4.1 - 2.5 = 1.6, and a quarter of 1.6 is 0.4.

solutions.reliable: The distance from P to Q is 4.1 - 2.5 = 1.6. One quarter of 1.6 is 0.4. Starting at P and moving 0.4 towards Q gives 2.5 + 0.4 = 2.9. Check: the halfway point is 3.3, and 2.9 is halfway between 2.5 and 3.3, so it is one quarter of the way. The transferable idea: a fraction of the way from one point to another is the start plus that fraction of the gap.
solutions.elegant: Halve twice: halfway from 2.5 to 4.1 is 3.3, and halfway from 2.5 to 3.3 is 2.9.

whyOnTest: Number line questions test the difference between a distance and a position, and decimal care with fractions of a gap.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
